- prompts/mode-workflow-failure-heal.txt: lines 168-175 (the new "Hard rules:" bullet: "Never suggest adding a `files_touched` block that lists only the rejected automation paths to an issue that has none: the scope guard then enforces that block, and every other file the change needs is rejected as out of scope.") | severity=NIT | confidence=3

  WHY: An LLM that reads the rule literally could refuse to suggest a `files_touched: ['.github/workflows/x.yml']` block for a single-path automation change on an issue that has none, leaving the diagnosis with no actionable fix.

  Requirement: "The report makes no extra GitHub API call; reports from older reporters show the author as unknown." (changelog.d/7157-heal-scope-blocked-author.md, line 6)
  Expected change site: changelog.d/7157-heal-scope-blocked-author.md, in the operator-facing paragraph.
  Evidence of absence: The reporter script (scripts/workflow_failure_heal_report.sh, lines 165-172) now runs `gh_retry gh api user --jq .login` for `ai:scope-blocked` reports. The previous reporter did NOT make this call when only `ai:scope-blocked` was set (the prior condition was `ai:needs-human` only). For a pure `ai:scope-blocked` report, this is one extra authenticated GitHub API call per report compared to the prior implementation. The README's framing ("the one `gh api user` read the `ai:needs-human` checks already make") is similarly misleading for `ai:scope-blocked`-only reports.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py, Location: line 309, the constant `_SCOPE_AUTHOR_LOGIN_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,38}(\[bot\])?$")`
  Issue: The regex allows up to 44 characters (1 + 38 + 5 for the optional `[bot]` suffix), trailing hyphens, and consecutive hyphens, while GitHub's documented login rules cap usernames at 39 characters total and disallow leading, trailing, or consecutive hyphens. The accompanying comment claims it "matches the GitHub login pattern". Forged payloads could supply a 39-44 character "login" ending in hyphens that pass validation and end up in the diagnosis prompt. (No authorization decision keys off the value; this is defense-in-depth.)
  Suggested minimal fix: Tighten the regex to enforce a final non-hyphen character and the documented 39-character total, e.g. `re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9]|-(?!-)){0,37}$|^[A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9]|-(?!-)){0,33}\[bot\]$")`, and update the comment.
  Estimated lines changed: 2
